test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts-P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

Climate change remains one of the biggest challenges of our time.

P. Shifting rainfall patterns are already affecting agriculture.

Q. Melting glaciers are disrupting water supplies in many regions.

R. Its impacts are visible across the globe.

S. Rising sea levels threaten low-lying coastal areas.

6. Urgent global collaboration is essential to tackle it.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The passage begins with the idea that **climate change is a global challenge**, and the following sentences describe the **visible impacts** of climate change around the world.
 
• **Sentence R** – “Its impacts are visible across the globe.” naturally follows the introduction, as it broadens the context by confirming the global effect.
 
• **Sentence Q** – “Melting glaciers are disrupting water supplies in many regions.” logically comes next, as it gives a specific example of the global impact mentioned earlier.
 
• **Sentence P** – “Shifting rainfall patterns are already affecting agriculture.” continues by explaining another consequence of climate change after melting glaciers.
 
• **Sentence S** – “Rising sea levels threaten low-lying coastal areas.” concludes the series of examples, completing the list of visible impacts before the final statement that calls for global collaboration.
 
• Hence, the most logical and coherent order of sentences is **RQPS**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

“Climate change remains one of the biggest challenges of our time. Its impacts are visible across the globe. Melting glaciers are disrupting water supplies in many regions. Shifting rainfall patterns are already affecting agriculture. Rising sea levels threaten low-lying coastal areas. Urgent global collaboration is essential to tackle it.”
